posts.author: Patrick Moorhead
posts.text:
$QCOM off the call and not in the release: data center is now a supply question, not a demand question. Upside beyond the $5B FY27 target is constrained by supply, and two hyperscalers at scale make up most of the $5B, both running into FY28 and FY29.

Top 5 things the call added:
1. High-bandwidth compute is beating its design target in the lab: ~0.3 picojoules per bit vs 0.5, yields above plan, strongest on decode.
2. Gross margin has a number now: once price increases land, the baseline returns to the low end of 48% to 50%, before custom silicon dilution.
3. As I said in July, China troughed. June was the bottom for China Android, with growth in September and December. Samsung share baseline: 70%+, up from 50%.
4. Earlier today I wanted SpaceX deal size and revenue timing. We got timing: revenue starts exiting FY27, mostly FY28. No size yet which is understandable.
5. Auto's 5th-gen platform carries 8x the silicon content of 3rd-gen cars on the road. The growth is share, not pre-buys.

@Qualcomm
posts.ko: 퀄컴 콜 핵심: 데이터센터는 이제 수요가 아니라 공급 문제, FY27 50억 달러 목표의 대부분은 하이퍼스케일러 2곳

posts.author: Patrick Moorhead
posts.text:
$ARM fiscal Q2: BEAT and raise, but down ~3% after hours.. The market is selling royalties: +8% vs a low-teens guide, my test before the print.

The numbers:
-Revenue $1.44B, +27% YoY, vs $1.38B est: BEAT
-Non-GAAP EPS $0.52 vs $0.47 est, $0.51 whisper: BEAT
-Royalties $670M, +8% YoY, vs low-teens guide: MISS
-Licensing $773M, +50% YoY, vs ~30% guide: BEAT
-Q3 guide $1.54B vs $1.52B est: BEAT

Takeaways:
1. Royalty growth fell to 8% from 22%. Data center doubled; phones went backwards. New quarter, new royalty explanation and that's OK.
2. Licensing is Arm's book-to-bill, royalties years out, and it lifted non-GAAP operating margin to 44.2%.
3. AGI CPU is supply-gated, and "up to $2B" is mostly FY28. (no surprise here they could sell a lot more)
4. Arm's top-hyperscaler server share passed 50%; Graviton commitments rose 20x. The target is x86, not licensees.
5. H1 royalties grew ~15%. July's high-teens outlook needs ~20% in H2. My math.

@Arm
posts.ko: 암 실적 서프라이즈·가이던스 상향에도 로열티 +8%(가이던스 미달)로 시간외 약 -3%

posts.author: Patrick Moorhead
posts.text:
$COHR FQ1: BEAT and raise, up ~8% after hours after a 56% slide since June. The market is buying >60% FY27 growth.

The numbers:
-Revenue $2.37B, +56% pro forma, vs $2.30B est: BEAT
-Non-GAAP EPS $2.09 vs $1.97 est: BEAT
-Non-GAAP gross margin 40.6% vs 40.5% guide: MEET
-FQ2 guide ~$2.65B vs $2.53B est: BEAT
-FY27 growth >60% vs ~50% street: BEAT

Takeaways:
1. In the deck: a ~$20B, five-year PhotonLink deal from early CY2028. As I said Monday, Marvell buying Lumentum makes Coherent the neutral supplier.
2. In CPO, what surrounds the laser is as big an opportunity as the laser. PhotonLink sells all of it.
3. In August I said capacity and cash matter. InP output doubled a quarter early. Operating cash flow was -$93M on $776M capex.
4. The CFO credits pricing and cost, targeting >45% gross margin by end of CY2028. Lasers are the choke point.
5. By my math, >60% FY27 growth will need ~$3B a quarter in 2H, not one $3B quarter by June.

@CoherentCorp
